title: Scalar compatibility of the smooth purity pullback exchange
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p^a}$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, and use the rational constructible categories $\mathcal C_E(W)=D^b_c(W,E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], the twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], the derived pullbacks and exceptional inverse images of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and the exact scalar extensions $T_W=T_{L/E,W}$ of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Write $G_{h,E}=Rh_E^!$ and $H_{h,E}=Lh_E^*(-)(d_h)[2d_h]$ for a smooth separated $h$ of pure relative dimension $d_h$. Let $\gamma_{h,E}:H_{h,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{h,E}$ be the rationalization of the simultaneous integral purity family of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], as in [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]. Denote by $b_{h,K}:T_{\mathrm{source}(h)}G_{h,E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{h,L}T_{\mathrm{target}(h)}K$ the rationalized counit-normalized comparison specified in that integral scalar-naturality statement.

Let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X'&\xrightarrow{u}&X\\ f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{v}&Y\end{array}$$
be a Cartesian square of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with $f$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$, $v$ an arbitrary $k$-morphism, and $K\in\mathcal C_E(Y)$. Then $f'$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] and separated of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Use the scalar pullback comparisons
$$p_{h,M}:T_{\mathrm{source}(h)}Lh_E^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh_L^*T_{\mathrm{target}(h)}M$$
of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. For $R=E,L$, let $\operatorname{Ex}_R^{!,\mathrm{sm}}:Lu_R^*G_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{f',R}Lv_R^*$ be the smooth exchange obtained by integral reconstruction and rationalization of the purity composite of [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange], as specified in [def-pur-conventions, prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence]. Define
$$\beta_{A,K}=Lu_L^*(b_{f,K})\circ p_{u,G_{f,E}K}:T_{X'}Lu_E^*G_{f,E}K\longrightarrow Lu_L^*G_{f,L}T_YK,$$
$$\beta_{B,K}=G_{f',L}(p_{v,K})\circ b_{f',Lv_E^*K}:T_{X'}G_{f',E}Lv_E^*K\longrightarrow G_{f',L}Lv_L^*T_YK.$$
Then the actual smooth exchange satisfies the scalar equation
$$\beta_{B,K}\circ T_{X'}(\operatorname{Ex}_{E,K}^{!,\mathrm{sm}})=\operatorname{Ex}_{L,T_YK}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}\circ\beta_{A,K}.$$
This is an equality of natural transformations in $K$, with the unit, successive coefficient-extension and shift identifications specified by the scalar comparisons above.

proof.text: All four schemes are Noetherian and finite-dimensional: apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to their structure morphisms over the field $k$, and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Since $\ell\ne p$, $\ell$ is invertible on them. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] and [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $f'$ is smooth separated finite type of pure relative dimension $d$, including when $X'$ is empty. Thus both $f$ and $f'$ satisfy the geometric hypotheses of the simultaneous purity family. The raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] gives an integral representative for every rational object. The characterization [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] identifies that integral category with the one in purity, and [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] gives its uniform finite-Tor condition. Pullbacks used below preserve integral constructibility by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], so this applies also to $Lv_E^*K$. No restriction on $v$ beyond the displayed scheme setting is used.

proof.text:
For $h=f,f'$, denote by $a_{h,M}:T H_{h,E}M\to H_{h,L}TM$ the rationalization of the comparison $a$ in [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality]. Its purity square, after applying [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport], is
$$b_{h,M}\circ T(\gamma_{h,E,M})=\gamma_{h,L,TM}\circ a_{h,M}.\tag{P}$$
Here $b$ is exactly the counit-normalized comparison named in the item, not an independently chosen isomorphism. By [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity], these rationalized $\gamma$ are the purity maps used in the item. Localization preserves the equality on each integral representative and extends naturality to localized morphisms. It also preserves the unit, successive-extension and shift equations in the simultaneous integral family. In particular (P) holds at every rational $M$ required below.

proof.text:
Write $D_W^R(M)=M(d)[2d]$ and let $q_{W,M}:T_WD_W^E M\to D_W^L T_WM$ be the tensor/twist/shift comparison. The comparison $a$ of step 2 factors, by its specified pullback/tensor/twist/shift construction, as
$$a_{h,M}=D_{\mathrm{source}(h)}^L(p_{h,M})\circ q_{\mathrm{source}(h),Lh_E^*M}.$$
Let $z^R_{u,M}:Lu_R^*D_X^R M\to D_{X'}^R Lu_R^*M$ be the pullback/twist/shift comparison occurring in the definition of the middle arrow. The tensor comparisons commute with scalar extension by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. The twist-line pullback of [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists] commutes with scalar extension directly from [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]: for $d\geq0$ both routes send a tensor of $d$ roots-of-unity sections with coefficient $e\in E$ to the same pulled-back tensor with coefficient the image of $e$ in $L$; for $d=0$ this is the unit map. Tensor balancing gives equality of these line maps. Together with the shift comparisons this gives
$$z^L_{u,T_XM}\circ Lu_L^*(q_{X,M})\circ p_{u,D_X^E M}=D_{X'}^L(p_{u,M})\circ q_{X',Lu_E^*M}\circ T_{X'}(z^E_{u,M}).\tag{Z}$$
This uses the scalar compatibility of the actual tensor comparison, not detection of equality from unrelated finite reductions.

proof.text:
Put $U_R=Lu_R^*Lf_R^*$ and $V_R=Lf'_R{}^*Lv_R^*$. Let $t_R:U_R\to V_R$ be the untwisted comparison of the commutative square, namely $c_{f',v}\circ c_{u,f}^{-1}$. Here these are the transported pullback composition comparisons in [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange]. Define
$$P_U=Lu_L^*(p_f)\circ p_{u,Lf_E^*(-)},\qquad P_V=Lf'_L{}^*(p_v)\circ p_{f',Lv_E^*(-)}.$$
The composition compatibility of the canonical scalar pullback comparisons in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], applied first to $(u,f)$ and then to $(f',v)$, gives
$$P_V\circ T_{X'}(t_E)=t_L\circ P_U.\tag{C}$$
Indeed the two composition squares have the common third side $p_{f\circ u}=p_{v\circ f'}$. Reverse the first composition square (all its arrows are isomorphisms) and paste the second. This proves (C) for the specified comparisons.

source.place: base-change coherence transported along the same exact functors; explicit scalar-square calculation for the purity composite

proof.text:
Let $m_R:Lu_R^*H_{f,R}\to H_{f',R}Lv_R^*$ denote the middle arrow of the transported purity composite. Thus
$$m_R=D_{X'}^R(t_R)\circ z^R_{u,Lf_R^*(-)}.$$
Set
$$r_A=Lu_L^*(a_f)\circ p_{u,H_{f,E}(-)},\qquad r_B=H_{f',L}(p_v)\circ a_{f',Lv_E^*(-)}.$$
Using the factorization of $a$ in step 3 and naturality of $q$, equation (Z) says
$$z^L_{u,Lf_L^*T_Y(-)}\circ r_A=D_{X'}^L(P_U)\circ q_{X',U_E(-)}\circ T_{X'}(z^E_{u,Lf_E^*(-)}),$$
whereas $r_B=D_{X'}^L(P_V)\circ q_{X',V_E(-)}$. Therefore naturality of $q$ at $t_E$, followed by (C), gives
$$r_B\circ T_{X'}(m_E)=m_L\circ r_A.\tag{M}$$
These identities are pastings of (Z), (C), and naturality; in particular no exceptional base-change theorem is used to identify this middle arrow.

proof.text:
Let $s_R=(Lu_R^*\gamma_{f,R})^{-1}$. Invert the isomorphisms in (P) for $h=f$ to obtain
$$a_{f,K}\circ T_X(\gamma_{f,E,K}^{-1})=\gamma_{f,L,T_YK}^{-1}\circ b_{f,K}.$$
Naturality of $p_u$ at $\gamma_{f,E,K}^{-1}$, followed by this equality, gives
$$r_{A,K}\circ T_{X'}(s_{E,K})=s_{L,T_YK}\circ\beta_{A,K}.\tag{A}$$
In detail the left side is
$$Lu_L^*(a_{f,K})\circ Lu_L^*T_X(\gamma_{f,E,K}^{-1})\circ p_{u,G_{f,E}K},$$
which becomes $Lu_L^*(\gamma_{f,L,T_YK}^{-1})\circ Lu_L^*(b_{f,K})\circ p_{u,G_{f,E}K}$, exactly the right side.

proof.text:
For the final purity factor, use (P) at $h=f'$ and $M=Lv_E^*K$, and then naturality of $\gamma_{f',L}$ at the actual morphism $p_{v,K}:T_{Y'}Lv_E^*K\to Lv_L^*T_YK$. This yields
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_{B,K}\circ T_{X'}(\gamma_{f',E,Lv_E^*K})
&=G_{f',L}(p_{v,K})\circ\gamma_{f',L,T_{Y'}Lv_E^*K}\circ a_{f',Lv_E^*K}\\
&=\gamma_{f',L,Lv_L^*T_YK}\circ H_{f',L}(p_{v,K})\circ a_{f',Lv_E^*K}\\
&=\gamma_{f',L,Lv_L^*T_YK}\circ r_{B,K}.\tag{B}
\end{aligned}$$
The naturality used here is the rationalization of the natural transformation in [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], extended to all rational morphisms by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport].

source.place: base-change coherence transported along the same exact functors; explicit scalar-square calculation for the purity composite

proof.text:
The finite exchange is defined in [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange] by $\gamma_{f'}\circ m\circ s$. The reconstruction of [prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence] and the rational transport [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] carry that specified composite to the actual $\operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}_R$ of the item, since functors preserve composition and inverses. Thus (B), (M), and (A), in order, give
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_B\circ T_{X'}(\operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}_E)
&=\gamma_{f',L}\circ r_B\circ T_{X'}(m_E)\circ T_{X'}(s_E)\\
&=\gamma_{f',L}\circ m_L\circ r_A\circ T_{X'}(s_E)\\
&=\gamma_{f',L}\circ m_L\circ s_L\circ\beta_A
=\operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}_L\circ\beta_A.
\end{aligned}$$
Every component here is evaluated at $K$, and the $L$-exchange at $T_YK$. This is the asserted component equation.

proof.text: All the factors in (P), (Z), (C), and the purity composite are natural in their arguments, so the component equation of step 8 is an equality of natural transformations. The unit and successive coefficient-extension equations for $a,b$ are those of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], rationalized as in step 2; those for $p$ are in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The tensor comparisons respect associators and units and commute with scalar extension by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Under one more extension, substitute these equations for each factor in the displayed pasting: intermediate associators occur consecutively with their inverses and cancel. The remaining external associators are precisely those of $\beta_A$ and $\beta_B$. For the identity extension all these factors are identities. The same substitution with the shift comparisons, which the cited $a,b,p$ respect, gives the shifted equation. Twists use tensor powers of a degree-zero line, so the comparison (Z) introduces no extra shift sign. This proves the last coherence clause with exactly the specified identifications.

The delivery has no new nodes and leaves the statement unchanged. Ex is the purity composite of def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange, not a mate; v is arbitrary; and gamma is the rationalized simultaneous family the parent fixes, so Ex and gamma use the same lift. I recomputed by hand the scalar-compatibility equations the steps call (C), (M), (A), (B) and the final pasting. Step 3's factorization a = D(p) after q is a sound reading of 'the pullback, tensor, twist and shift comparison' (both orders agree by naturality of q). The twist-line check holds because O_F(d) is generated locally by the image of Z_l(1)^d tensor 1. Step 1's hypotheses hold: Spec k is Noetherian, the schemes are finite-dimensional, l != p, residue-tor gives D^b_c = D^b_ctf, and Lv^*K stays integral-constructible. Small cases checked: E=L, v=id, d=0, X' empty, K=0. No SGA source, no cycle, and the searches are recorded (one Loogle pattern honestly marked invalid). I accept the off-unit tool_uses; the two Mathlib leaves and lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso, which is on route, need none.
